event: Before light or cold, a woman's voice, thin with distance, repeats: Open your eyes.
Wake up, Link. The name lands somewhere inside him and fits, though he does not know why.
Water runs off him as he lies on curved stone; his fingers move, and his lungs draw stale air.
His eyes open on a blue ceiling of carved patterns, glowing and pulsing slowly.
His body takes stock of itself: heartbeat, lungs, a dry mouth. He swallows.
He sits up, heavy, as the last luminous blue water drains from the basin under him.
He stares a long time at his calloused hands, the only proof he existed before now.
The small oval chamber holds two chests banded with orange light and a pedestal by a sealed door.
He swings his legs over the basin's edge, and his knees nearly buckle as he stands.
His hands know the chests' latches: inside are a faded pale blue shirt and trousers.

changes.note: Link takes the old shirt from the first chest
Link takes the trousers from the second chest

event: He dresses in the blue light, fumbling the fastenings; both fit, both are thin, and he is not warm.
On the pedestal lies a smooth dark rectangle that fits his palm exactly, warm and humming.

changes.note: Link lifts the Sheikah Slate from its pedestal

event: A two-note chime; the screen lights with an eye, then text: Sheikah Slate activated.
The Slate shows hearts 3/3, one stamina wheel, four locked rune slots and no map.

changes.note: The Slate shows Link's hearts at 3/3: twelve quarter-hearts at most

event: Hearts, stamina, runes mean nothing to him; he touches his chest and feels the beat there.
The sealed door grinds open on a blue-lit corridor, with a thin line of daylight at its end.
He walks barefoot up the warming corridor, the Slate fastened at his hip, humming.
The corridor ends at a cliff: he steps from carved stone onto warm, thick, living grass.
Wind hits him under an enormous sky, and the drop makes him step back.
Below: green fields, forests, ruins half-swallowed by grass, and a temple with a broken spire.
Far to the northeast a mountain burns with a dull orange glow, as it always has.
Straight ahead stands a castle, coiled in slow purple-black tendrils.
He stares at it, his heart beating fast, from fear or recognition or both.
The air smells of pine, river mud, sulfur and distance; his breath shows in the cold morning.
A small brown bird darts past his cheek; he flinches, arms half-raised, and feels foolish.
The Slate chimes and shows a map: one pulsing blip, his own, on a place with no name.
By the temple below, smoke rises from a campfire, and a small dark figure stands beside it.
He looks back at the castle and its coiling darkness, then starts down the hill.
The world is loud with sounds he cannot name; only on the third call does he place birdsong.
Hungry, he pulls a red apple from a gnarled tree and bites before he wonders if it is safe.
He eats three apples standing under the tree, juice on his chin, then walks on.
Near the hill's foot he picks up a fallen branch, and his grip settles on it like a weapon's.

changes.note: Link picks up a fallen tree branch

event: The branch is light and dry and will not last. He does not know how he knows that.
A greasy, charred smell, then grunts and high barks: neither human sounds nor animal ones.
He drops into a silent crouch in the grass, the branch held close, without deciding to.
Through the grass: a crude camp round a fire, a rack of meat, apples, and a sleeping platform.
Two squat, clay-skinned creatures sit at the fire, one with a bone club; a third sleeps.
He counts three, reads fifteen paces of open ground, and knows he should go around.
The club-creature sees him and barks; the second turns, and the sleeper rolls to its feet.
He closes in four strides, turns aside from a swing at his ribs, and drives the branch home.
He strikes again and again, footwork precise, breath controlled; his body has done this before.
On the fourth swing the branch cracks in two, and half of it spins away into the dirt.
Empty-handed, he drops under the next swing and seizes a fallen creature's bone club.

changes.note: Link takes up a fallen bokoblin's bone club

event: He puts down the slow sleeper first, then the fire-tender, then the first one, behind him.
Silence, then the fire; his pulse hammers, and his scraped, bleeding hands shake.
The Slate chimes: damage received, four quarter-hearts lost; one heart line is shorter.

changes.note: Damage received in the camp fight: four quarter-hearts lost

event: The creatures come apart into dark smoke, leaving their weapons and acrid scraps of hide.
He takes their bow and quiver of stone-tipped arrows, an apple per pocket, and pale mushrooms.

changes.note: Link takes the bokoblins' bow and quiver

event: His legs give; he sits by their fire, eats their apples, and turns the bone club over.
He looks a long while at the broken branch lying in two pieces.
Farther down by the broken temple, a hooded old man in a dark cloak watches a fire.
He looks up, sharp and patient-eyed: "Well. You're awake."
Link stops at the firelight, scraped and barefoot, club in hand; the old man nods.
"Sit. You look like you've had a difficult introduction to the Plateau."
Link sits. The fire's warmth is the best thing yet, because someone built it before he came.
The old man turns an apple over the flames: "Cooking. Heat and patience."
Link eats the baked apple in four bites; the old man watches, caught between amusement and grief.
"You eat like you haven't in a while," the old man says quietly.
He tosses a second apple underhand; Link catches it one-handed without looking.
The Plateau has been sealed some time, he says, and Link came from the cave on the ridge.
Link says nothing; language sits behind his sternum, heavy and unformed.
He points east to an amber glow: one of four shrines on the Plateau, each with a trial.
Bring me what you find in them, he says, and I will give you something to leave by.
He shows a folded paraglider: the only way off the Plateau is to fly or to fall.

changes.note: The old man shows the paraglider he keeps in his cloak

event: "In the morning, perhaps." The night is cold, and Link is not especially prepared.
An owl calls behind the temple; for a moment his face is very old and very tired.
"Rest. The world will still be here in the morning."
Night falls; the old man sits wrapped in his cloak across the fire, perhaps asleep.
Link holds the Slate in his lap; its eye glows, steady and patient, watching him.
He turns the longer half of the broken branch over, then lays it in the fire.
He feeds in the second piece, and it burns faster than the first.

changes.note: The broken branch's two halves burn in the fire

event: Better weapons will break too, he knows; the stars are out in patterns he does not know.
He cannot see the castle in the dark, but he feels it, a weight on the horizon.
Cold, alive and alone, he hears the voice again, faintly: someone present at a distance.
Someone believes he will get up tomorrow. He closes his eyes.
